correctness.rationale: The Gamma-Dirichlet disintegration yields independent transfer proportions Dirichlet(2,2,1) after first-choice conditioning. The Jacobian gives f(d)=1-3d²+2|d|³; integrating on (δ,1) is exactly (1-δ)^3(1+δ)/2. Posterior group shares Dirichlet(n_i+5) concentrate under large first-choice-only polling while transfer ratios do not, proving non-identifiability. Standalone exact-rational and independent Gamma Monte Carlo checks passed.

originality.rationale: Examined the complete available online text of arXiv:2606.31022, particularly original modeling and simulation results, and the older unconditional IRV catalog. Compared explicit statements and their implications; neither states the fifteen-type first-choice-only posterior quartic, cubic boundary rate and infinite-poll residual uncertainty. The result uses classical Dirichlet neutrality and possible implicit or unindexed derivations remain real risks.
residual_risks: No novelty assertion against inaccessible or unindexed mathematical writing; an unlocated general explicit Dirichlet ratio/difference formula may imply this result.
Flat typewise Dirichlet priors on truncated and complete ballots have different induced beliefs; the comparator is not controlled for prior changes.
Sources were inspected for the exact result, but originality is not an independent literature certification.

value.rationale: The exact conditional probability is a natural quantitative identifiable/non-identifiable boundary for using cheaper first-choice-only polls under a recently proposed RCV Bayesian model. It gives a strictly positive residual winner error at infinite sample sizes without first-choice majority, an explicit quartic formula, a sharp cubic threshold exponent, and an explicit comparison of two ballot universes. These are decision-relevant structural features beyond generic conjugacy or an arbitrarily chosen numeric example.
